lesson.text: Quick memory: what is an event? (Something that happens, like a tap, that starts some steps.) Today: programs that make choices.
A condition is a question with only two answers: true or false (yes or no). Is it raining? Is the score more than 10? Programs check conditions to choose what to do.
IF runs its steps only when the condition is true. IF it is raining, take an umbrella. When it isn't raining, the program skips that step.
IF … ELSE chooses one of two ways. IF it is raining, take an umbrella; ELSE (otherwise), wear a sun hat. One of them always happens, never both.
Conditions can compare numbers. With a score of 12, 12 > 10 is true: Gold star! With a score of 10, 10 > 10 is false (10 is not more than 10): Keep going!
The robot can choose too: IF a wall is ahead, TURN RIGHT, ELSE FORWARD. Repeat it, and the robot walks on until it meets a wall, then turns.
Games use conditions all the time: IF your player is in water, swim; IF it is night, the sky goes dark; IF it is night in a Survivor world, the monsters come out.
Try it in the world: play IF … ELSE with a friend in your world: IF they place a red block, you jump; ELSE you spin round. Next: variables, which keep a score.

exercises.prompt: Which of these is a condition, a question with a true or false answer?
exercises.hint: Can you answer it with yes or no?
exercises.explain: Is the door open? has only two answers, yes or no: a condition.

exercises.prompt: With IF … ELSE, both parts can run at the same time.
exercises.hint: How many ways does IF … ELSE choose between?
exercises.explain: False: the condition is true or false, so only one part runs.

exercises.prompt: It is sunny today. What does this program choose?
exercises.hint: Is the condition true or false today?
exercises.explain: It is not raining, so the condition is false and the ELSE part runs: trainers.

exercises.prompt: Sort these: a condition (a yes or no question), or an instruction?
exercises.hint: Can you answer it with yes or no, or is it telling you to do something?
exercises.explain: Conditions ask a yes or no question. Instructions tell you what to do.

exercises.hint: Put 15 into the condition. Is 15 less than 10?
exercises.explain: temp is 15, and 15 < 10 is false, so the ELSE part runs: Wear a T-shirt.
10 > 10 is false: 10 is not more than 10. The ELSE part runs: Keep going!

exercises.prompt: Match each condition to what to do.
exercises.hint: Which action makes sense when each is true?
exercises.explain: Dark: the lamp. Full bath: the tap off. Red light: stop. Thirsty: water.

exercises.prompt: IF gems ≥ 5, open the gate. With exactly 5 gems, the gate opens.
exercises.hint: ≥ means more than, or equal to.
exercises.explain: True: 5 ≥ 5 is true, because 5 is equal to 5.

exercises.prompt: It is not raining. Which way does the flowchart go?
exercises.hint: Follow the arrow for the answer to the diamond's question.
choices: Wear a sun hat, then Go out
Take an umbrella, then Go out
Take an umbrella and wear a sun hat
exercises.explain: The answer to Is it raining? is no, so follow the no arrow: Wear a sun hat, then Go out.

exercises.hint: Go down the program line by line. At each IF, is the condition true or false? Only one SAY runs.
exercises.explain: temp is 30. 30 > 25 is true, so it says Hot and skips the ELSE part.

exercises.hint: Go down the program line by line. At each IF, is the condition true or false? Only one SAY runs.
exercises.explain: temp is 8. 8 > 25 is false: go to ELSE. 8 > 12 is false too: it says Cold.

exercises.prompt: Which condition opens the gate only when there are 10 gems or more?
exercises.hint: Try each with exactly 10 gems, and with 9.
exercises.explain: gems ≥ 10 is true for 10 and more, false for 9. gems > 10 would keep the gate shut with exactly 10.

exercises.prompt: The robot runs REPEAT 4 TIMES: IF a wall is ahead, TURN RIGHT, ELSE FORWARD. How many squares does it move?
exercises.hint: Follow it round by round. Look at the square in front of the robot each time.
exercises.explain: Round 1: FORWARD. Round 2: FORWARD. Round 3: a wall, so TURN RIGHT. Round 4: FORWARD. 3 squares.

exercises.prompt: gems is 6. Sort these conditions: true or false?
exercises.hint: Put 6 in place of gems in each one.

exercises.prompt: IF score > 10, SAY Gold star!, ELSE SAY Keep going!. With a score of 11, it says both.
exercises.hint: How many parts of IF … ELSE run?
exercises.explain: False: 11 > 10 is true, so it says only Gold star!

exercises.prompt: A number starts at 7. IF it is even, add 1; ELSE add 2. What is the number now?
exercises.hint: Is 7 even or odd? Then follow the right part.
exercises.explain: 7 is odd, so the condition is false and the ELSE part adds 2: 7 + 2 = 9.

exercises.prompt: temp is 20. Sort the conditions: true or false?
exercises.hint: Put 20 in place of temp and check each one.
exercises.explain: True: 20 < 25, 20 = 20 and 20 > 19. False: 20 > 25, 20 ≥ 21 and 20 < 20 (20 is not less than itself).

exercises.prompt: IF score > 10, add 5 gold, ELSE add 1 gold. Three players score 12, 8 and 10. How much gold is added in all?
exercises.hint: Check the condition for each score. Careful with exactly 10!
exercises.explain: 12 > 10 is true: 5 gold. 8 > 10 is false: 1 gold. 10 > 10 is false: 1 gold. In all: 5 + 1 + 1 = 7 gold.
